A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RT-ER and JTDMoE work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet experiments, including adversarial evaluations, training curves and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds ImageNet results, an alternative MoE architecture evaluation and a routing-stability observation.

M1.justification: The RT-ER loss, linear dual-model combination and alternating JTDMoE training procedure remain unchanged in Equations (2), (3), (10) and Algorithm 1. Appendix A.2 clarifies architecture placement and tests another configuration without revising the proposed algorithms.

E1.justification: v3 adds large-scale ImageNet classification experiments in Appendix A.6, extending coverage beyond the retained CIFAR-10 and TinyImageNet benchmarks. This substantially broadens the scale of the evaluated data, while retaining the image-classification task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ST, AT, TRADES, AdvMoE and the pre-trained dual-model baseline. ImageNet reuses AT and TRADES; the additional transformer-block architecture check does not introduce a competing robustification method.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation with MoE layers replacing transformer-block MLPs in Appendix A.2 and a ViT/ImageNet configuration in A.6. The original attack budgets, training schedules and accuracy metrics remain unchanged. Precise settings for the new evaluations are only sparsely specified.

E4.justification: Section 3 newly reports that expert-targeted perturbations preserve expert selection in 98% of cases. Appendix A.2 additionally checks whether expert vulnerability persists with MoE layers inside transformer blocks. Existing routing, expert-count, beta and alpha analyses remain; the margin analysis is relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The added results follow the existing practice of reporting individual accuracy percentages.

E6.justification: v3 adds a large-scale benchmark result set: Table 10 reports ImageNet SA/RA of 68.38%/56.16% for RT-ER, 60.32%/44.64% for AT and 61.94%/45.54% for TRADES. It also adds architecture-check results and the 98% routing-stability finding. Matched original results remain unchanged, including the margin values moved from v1 Table 9 to v3 Table 5.

T1.justification: Definitions 5.1–5.2, Assumption 5.3, Theorems 5.4–5.5 and their Appendix A.1 proofs are unchanged. The new discussion explains applicability and the existing alpha restriction without introducing a new formal assumption, bound or proof.

C1.justification: The expanded conclusion explicitly claims scalability across models and datasets, broadening v1's concluding claim of effectiveness. The abstract and introduction retain the same central RT-ER, dual-model, theoretical-bound and joint-training contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds discussion of when the Lipschitz assumption applies to sparse, dense and soft routing, explains the certificate's alpha restriction, and proposes reduced overfitting as another reason to use KL divergence. It also interprets routing stability as supporting expert-targeted attacks and extends the vulnerability interpretation across architecture placements.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a public-code statement and repository address in the abstract. Appendix A.2 newly discloses that the default MoE replaces the classification layer. These improve access and implementation documentation, although detailed settings for the added experiments remain limited.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting architecture placement, including Videau et al., Chen et al. and He et al., and dense/soft routing discussion citing Zhang et al. and Puigcerver et al. The principal related-work section and positioning against existing robustness methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 locally expands explanatory passages and the conclusion, moves the margin discussion into Section 6.4, and introduces architecture and ImageNet appendix sections. It also corrects the running title and adds publication details and acknowledgements. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 moves the class-margin table from the appendix into the main text and adds ImageNet Table 10. Existing figures and tables retain their designs, with float relocation, renumbering and page reflow rather than substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The ImageNet results and alternative architecture check broaden empirical support, while the architecture disclosure and code-access information improve reproducibility documentation. However, the new experiments provide limited settings and sampling information, and the applicability discussion remains informal. These are useful but bounded gains; the central methods, proofs and previous results are unchanged.
